title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
abstract: arXiv:2610.04672v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have progressively evolved into the core of autonomous agents. Building on this progress, LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate multiple agents into a synergistic team to accomplish complex tasks that exceed the capabilities of individual agents. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and organized. Note that real-world collaboration is typically partially observable, where each agent can only access partial information about the environment due to physical or privacy-related constraints. However, many existing multi-agent benchmarks assume global observability, and leave limited support for systematically evaluating collaboration mechanisms. translated_title: MASBench：部分可观测性下基于大语言模型的多智能体协作基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已逐步演变为自主智能体的核心。在这一进展的基础上，基于LLM的多智能体系统（MAS）将多个智能体协调成一个协同团队，以完成超出单个智能体能力范围的复杂任务。此类系统的有效性不仅取决于智能体本身，还取决于协作机制的设计与组织方式。值得注意的是，现实世界中的协作通常是部分可观测的，即由于物理或隐私相关的限制，每个智能体只能获取环境中的部分信息。然而，许多现有的多智能体基准测试都假设全局可观测性，对系统性评估协作机制的支持十分有限。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了MASBench——一个在部分可观测约束下设计的多智能体协作基准测试。该基准由三个渐进……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了MASBench，首个在部分可观测性约束下系统评估基于大语言模型的多智能体系统协作机制的基准测试，填补了现有基准假设全局可观测性的空白。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces MASBench, the first benchmark designed to systematically evaluate collaboration mechanisms in LLM-based multi-agent systems under partially observable constraints, addressing the gap left by existing benchmarks that assume global observability.
